"""List books: GET /books returns stored books as JSON, in the order they were added."""

from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from app_server.book_service import list_books
from persistence import open_database

PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent


@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)
def store(monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    """Point the application at a fresh store per test, so listing starts from a known state."""
    url = f"sqlite:///{tmp_path / 'list-books.db'}"
    monkeypatch.setenv("DATABASE_URL", url)
    monkeypatch.delenv("DATABASE_PATH", raising=False)
    with open_database(url) as database:
        database.execute_script((PROJECT_ROOT / "schema.sql").read_text())
    return url


def _add(client, title: str, author: str = "List Author") -> None:
    assert client.post("/books", data={"title": title, "author": author}).status_code == 303


def test_get_books_answers_200_with_json(web_client):
    response = web_client.get("/books")

    assert response.status_code == 200
    assert response.is_json


def test_empty_store_lists_empty_array(web_client):
    assert web_client.get("/books").get_json() == []


def test_single_book_is_listed_with_id_title_and_author(web_client):
    _add(web_client, "Dune", "Frank Herbert")

    body = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert len(body) == 1
    assert body[0]["title"] == "Dune"
    assert body[0]["author"] == "Frank Herbert"
    assert isinstance(body[0]["id"], int)


def test_listed_book_carries_exactly_id_title_and_author(web_client):
    _add(web_client, "Dune", "Frank Herbert")

    body = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert set(body[0].keys()) == {"id", "title", "author"}


def test_several_books_are_listed_in_the_order_added(web_client):
    for title in ["Third-added-last", "A-first", "M-second"]:
        _add(web_client, title)

    body = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert [row["title"] for row in body] == ["Third-added-last", "A-first", "M-second"]


def test_listed_ids_ascend_across_the_sequence(web_client):
    for title in ["One", "Two", "Three", "Four"]:
        _add(web_client, title)

    ids = [row["id"] for row in web_client.get("/books").get_json()]

    assert ids == sorted(ids)
    assert len(set(ids)) == len(ids)


def test_book_added_after_a_listing_appears_at_the_end(web_client):
    _add(web_client, "First")
    web_client.get("/books")
    _add(web_client, "Second")

    body = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert [row["title"] for row in body] == ["First", "Second"]


def test_repeated_listing_returns_the_same_sequence(web_client):
    for title in ["Alpha", "Beta"]:
        _add(web_client, title)

    first = web_client.get("/books").get_json()
    second = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert first == second


def test_rejected_submission_is_not_listed(web_client):
    _add(web_client, "Kept")
    assert web_client.post("/books", data={"title": "", "author": "Nobody"}).status_code == 400

    body = web_client.get("/books").get_json()

    assert [row["title"] for row in body] == ["Kept"]


def test_listing_matches_the_persistence_store_order(web_client, store):
    for title in ["Store-one", "Store-two", "Store-three"]:
        _add(web_client, title)

    http_ids = [row["id"] for row in web_client.get("/books").get_json()]
    with open_database(store) as database:
        store_ids = [row.id for row in database.books.list()]

    assert http_ids == store_ids


def test_list_books_service_returns_rows_in_the_order_added(store):

        rows = list_books(database)

    assert [row.title for row in rows] == ["Service-one", "Service-two"]
    assert [row.id for row in rows] == sorted(row.id for row in rows)


def test_list_books_service_on_empty_store_returns_no_rows(store):
    with open_database(store) as database:
        assert list_books(database) == []

"""Book behavior for the ReadingList web application, free of any Flask dependency."""

from __future__ import annotations

from persistence import Database
from persistence.schema import BookRow


class BookRejected(ValueError):
    """A submission the application refuses to store; ``reason`` says why and ``field`` names the input."""

    def __init__(self, reason: str, field: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(reason)
        self.reason = reason
        self.field = field


class BookNotFound(LookupError):
    """A removal named an id that no stored book carries; ``book_id`` is that id."""

    def __init__(self, book_id: int) -> None:
        super().__init__(book_id)
        self.book_id = book_id


def add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:
    """Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row.

    Values are expected already trimmed by the caller. An empty title or author is refused
    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.
    """
    if not title:
        raise BookRejected("rejected: title is empty", field="title")
    if not author:
        raise BookRejected("rejected: author is empty", field="author")
    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)


def list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:
    """Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.

    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which
    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.
    """
    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)


def remove_book(database: Database, book_id: int) -> None:
    """Delete the stored book with ``book_id``; the remaining books keep their order.

    An id that no stored book carries is refused with ``BookNotFound`` before any write, so an
    unknown id never changes stored data.
    """
    if database.books.get(id=book_id) is None:
        raise BookNotFound(book_id)
    database.books.delete(id=book_id)

from werkzeug.wrappers import Response

bp = Blueprint("books", __name__)


def _database() -> Database:
    return current_app.extensions["database"]


def _reading_list(error: str | None = None) -> str:
    """Render the reading list page: the alert region, the add form, and the books in the order added."""
    return render_template("reading_list.html", books=list_books(_database()), error=error)


@bp.get("/")
def index() -> str:
    """Render the reading list page with every stored book in the order added."""
    return _reading_list()


@bp.get("/books")
def get_books() -> Response:
    """Return every stored book as a JSON array of ``id``, ``title`` and ``author``, oldest first."""
    return jsonify(

    )


@bp.post("/books")
def create_book() -> Response:
    """Add a book from the ``title`` and ``author`` form fields, then redirect to the start page.

    A refused submission answers 400: as JSON with ``error`` and ``field`` when the client asks
    for ``application/json``, otherwise as the reading list page with the reason in the alert region.
    """
    title = request.form.get("title", "").strip()
    author = request.form.get("author", "").strip()
    try:
        add_book(_database(), title=title, author=author)
    except BookRejected as rejected:
        if request.accept_mimetypes.best == "application/json":
            refused = jsonify(error=rejected.reason, field=rejected.field)
            refused.status_code = 400
            return refused
        return Response(
            _reading_list(error=rejected.reason),
            status=400,
            mimetype="text/html",
        )
    return redirect("/", code=303)


@bp.post("/books/<int:book_id>/delete")
def delete_book(book_id: int) -> Response:
    """Remove the book with ``book_id``, then redirect to the start page; an unknown id answers 404."""
    try:
        remove_book(_database(), book_id)
    except BookNotFound:
        abort(404)
    return redirect("/", code=303)

"""Book behavior for the ReadingList web application, free of any Flask dependency."""

from __future__ import annotations

from persistence import Database
from persistence.schema import BookRow


class BookRejected(ValueError):
    """A submission the application refuses to store; ``reason`` says why and ``field`` names the input."""

    def __init__(self, reason: str, field: str) -> None:
        super().__init__(reason)
        self.reason = reason
        self.field = field


class BookNotFound(LookupError):
    """A removal named an id that no stored book carries; ``book_id`` is that id."""

    def __init__(self, book_id: int) -> None:
        super().__init__(book_id)
        self.book_id = book_id


def add_book(database: Database, title: str, author: str) -> BookRow:
    """Store a book appended after every existing book and return the stored row.

    Values are expected already trimmed by the caller. An empty title or author is refused
    without touching the store, so a stored book always has both.
    """
    if not title:
        raise BookRejected("rejected: title is empty", field="title")
    if not author:
        raise BookRejected("rejected: author is empty", field="author")
    return database.books.create(title=title, author=author)


def list_books(database: Database) -> list[BookRow]:
    """Return every stored book in the order added, oldest first.

    The order is enforced here, by ascending id, rather than trusted to the store's select, which
    the generated persistence layer issues without an ORDER BY clause.
    """
    return sorted(database.books.list(), key=lambda row: row.id)


def remove_book(database: Database, book_id: int) -> None:
    """Delete the stored book with ``book_id``; the remaining books keep their order.

    An id that no stored book carries is refused with ``BookNotFound`` before any write, so an
    unknown id never changes stored data.
    """
    if database.books.get(id=book_id) is None:
        raise BookNotFound(book_id)
    database.books.delete(id=book_id)
